subject: Discrepancy in telemetry during June 1 partial degradation - SLA credit request
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Partial degradation seen Jun 1 (09:40-10:15 PT) - telemetry mismatch / credit request

Hi Marissa / Ben,

We saw a partial degradation on our end this morning between ~09:40-10:15 PT that impacted a subset of inference requests routed through your edge in us-west2. Our synthetic probes (attached) show a 4x latency spike and ~6% 5xx rate for a 35-minute window; however, the SLA dashboard and logs we pulled from the API don’t show the same breadth of impact.

We need Redwood to:- confirm the observed timeframe- provide server-side logs for the affected token batches- confirm whether this is attributable to a Redwood service, our CDN (Bifrost), or a transit/path issue

Per our contract (SLA section 4.2), we’re opening a request for credit unless this maps to an excluded third-party maintenance event. Attaching probe samples and a short screencap of our dashboard.

Attachments: acme_probe_samples.csv (csv)

Can you triage and confirm next steps?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform Ops, AcmeTech
ops@acmetech.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial degradation seen Jun 1 (09:40-10:15 PT) - telemetry mismatch / credit request

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the probe samples. I’ve opened an internal investigation and looped in Ben and Priyom to pull logs and correlate our ingress metrics to your timestamps.

Initial plan:
- Ben will extract the KV/cache and request traces for us-west2 between 09:30–10:30 PT and look for request-level errors or large tail latencies.
- Priyom will reconcile our service-level SLO counters with customer-facing probe data to identify sampling/aggregation differences.
- I’ll coordinate with our partnerships team to check whether upstream (Bifrost CDN) had any maintenance or incidents in that window.

Can you confirm which customer app(s) were impacted and whether you were seeing traffic routed through any custom PoPs? Also keeping this as an open escalation — we’ll aim to have a preliminary finding within 24 hours.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 10:03:27 -0700
Subject: RE: Partial degradation seen Jun 1 (09:40-10:15 PT) - initial log digs

Marissa / Priyom — I pulled the request traces and KV/cache latencies for the window (09:30–10:30 PT). Observations: 
- There’s a clear tail latency bump concentrated on clients routed via our edge-egress cluster in us-west2. P90->P99 delta jumps from ~120ms to ~720ms for affected shards.
- Error spike predominantly 502/504 from the edge (downstream integration failures).
- I also see intermittent upstream connection resets to the IP ranges that map to Bifrost (ASN: 64512) starting ~09:38 and resolving ~10:12. 

Excerpt from edge logs (anonymized):
[2027-06-01T09:38:41Z] edge-usw2-21 connection_reset peer=198.51.100.22 route=bifrost-po-7
[2027-06-01T09:41:03Z] edge-usw2-21 outbound_5xx count=12 backend=bifrost-po-7
[2027-06-01T10:10:58Z] edge-usw2-21 connection_recovery peer=198.51.100.22 route=bifrost-po-7

I’m attaching a scrubbed log dump (redwood_kv_logs_20270601.txt) and pushing a ticket to our partner channel. This looks like intermittent upstream instability rather than an internal scheduling/compilation regression. If Bifrost confirms maintenance or a circuit flap, this may fall under third-party exclusion, but we’ll confirm.

Attachments: redwood_kv_logs_20270601.txt

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: edgeops-support@bifrostcdn.net <edgeops-support@bifrostcdn.net>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmetech.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 07:15:50 -0700
Subject: RE: Partial degradation seen Jun 1 (09:40-10:15 PT) - Bifrost ticket 78942

Hi team,

Thanks for the report and the excerpted logs. Ticket 78942 has been created for the outage window you provided. Summary: scheduled reconfiguration in our us-west edge-aggregation cluster had an orchestration rollback at 09:36 PT which caused TCP session resets for a subset of peers (including netblock 198.51.100.0/24) until automatic failover stabilized at ~10:11 PT. We published a maintenance notice in our customer portal (link below) at 06:00 PT; however, the rollback was unanticipated and caused transient degradations.

We’re attaching the ticket PDF with timeline and upstream diagnostics. From Bifrost’s perspective this is an upstream maintenance incident; we’re happy to coordinate a joint statement for your audit.

Attachments: bifrost_ticket_78942.pdf
Related: https://status.bifrostcdn.net/incidents/78942

Regards,
Bifrost EdgeOps Support
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acmetech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial degradation seen Jun 1 (09:40-10:15 PT) - proposed resolution and next steps

Hi Sanjay — thanks for your patience while we pulled the traces and coordinated with Bifrost. Summary of findings:

- Impact window: 2027-06-01 09:38–10:11 PT (33 minutes) where we observed elevated latency and a brief 5xx spike tied to upstream TCP resets.
- Root cause: Bifrost orchestration rollback caused circuit instability for a subset of peers; corroborated by the Bifrost ticket 78942 and our edge log excerpts (attached).
- Classification: This aligns with a third-party upstream maintenance incident per SLA exclusion clauses.

Proposed customer outcome:
1) Offer a goodwill operational credit equal to 30% of the per-minute token charge for requests routed via the affected egress cluster during the window (we calculate this to be approximately one invoice line item). We’re treating this as an exception rather than an automatic SLA payout because the root cause is documented third-party maintenance.
2) Provide a joint incident summary (Redwood + Bifrost) for your audit/records.
3) Implement an immediate improvement to our probe-fanout mapping so customer-facing probes are included in our SLO visibility for similar future events.

If that is acceptable, I’ll draft the credit memo and route it through billing for you, and we’ll publish the joint incident note. If you prefer a formal SLA credit calculation instead of a goodwill credit, please say so and we’ll run the formal apportionment calculation.

Thanks again — quick Q: do you want the joint incident note publicly stamped (status page) or delivered as an audit artifact only?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
